question: Every segmented control is now the Mac's own. Is this what you wanted?
context: Filmed and photographed in the app on 2026-09-29: the Mac's own segmented control on macOS 26 is one track, accent-filled when the window is in front, and switches at once. The sheet and the film strip are in the audit.

options.label: Keep the Mac's own control
options.summary: Every row of side-by-side choices stays exactly as macOS draws it: one continuous track, the picked segment filled with your accent colour in the front window and grey behind, switching at once.
pros: It is the real system control, so it matches every other Mac app and follows every macOS update
Nothing of ours is drawn on it, so the picked word is always readable
cons: The picked segment is accent blue in the front window, not a glass pane
It switches at once rather than sliding
options.mitigation: Nothing to soften: this is the look and motion macOS gives its own apps.

options.label: Glass toolbar for View | Edit
options.summary: Give recording windows a real macOS toolbar so View | Edit sits in it the way Finder's view switcher does, in Liquid Glass. Panel rows and dialogs stay as they are now.
pros: The title bar switch gets the glass look Finder and Mail show
cons: A toolbar draws a bar across the top of the window, which the editor was built not to have
Only the title bar changes; panel rows still use the accent fill
options.mitigation: The bar can be transparent over the canvas, but it still takes height from the window.

options.label: Back to the drawn glass
options.summary: Put back the control we drew ourselves: a recessed rail with one pane of glass sliding to the picked segment.
pros: The selection slides and is a glass pane rather than a colour fill
cons: It is ours, not the Mac's: it produced the overshoot and the white-on-white history filter
options.mitigation: Its walks and films are still in history, so the known problems would be fixed first.
